title: When Fats put his on-the-spot tunes on paper
summary: Fats wrote tunes down only when he needed money, for whiskey rather than food, mostly before he had the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How fast did Fats get these things that you did on the stand, in print out? Did he write them down right away? Or did anybody write them down?
Aside from people writing on their cuffs?
No, no, no, they didn't. He didn't.
Did it wait 'til it was recorded, or something like that?

When -- that, or when he needed some money. (Laughs.) And after he got started with the band it was very seldom he needed money. This was more or less when he was alone by himself, with -- when he needed -- when he needed that extra buck.

I remember those stories back in the twenties, usually, when he turned out about -- what? -- one of those about every -- he wrote nine tunes for nine hamburgs, or something like that, one night. (Laughs.)
I doubt it was for -- it was for whiskey. He didn't write no tune for food.
